turnaround_reason: The CX/BPO leader de-rated to a low-single-digit multiple as the market prices AI displacing its core customer-service outsourcing. Thesis is that the fear is over-discounted for a ~$10B-revenue, FCF-generative platform that is itself deploying AI (iX Suite).
bullish_points: Absurdly cheap on forward earnings: fwd P/E ~2.4, P/B ~0.65, EV/EBITDA ~5.5 — pricing near-terminal decline
Still growing modestly (revenue +1.9% cc in Q1 2026) and FCF-positive (~$776M TTM)
Analyst consensus 'Buy' (7 buy / 2 hold), target mean ~$35 vs ~$29 — decent upside if AI fear normalizes
iX Suite technology contracts growing — company is trying to be an AI beneficiary, not just a victim
bearish_points: AI disruption to voice/chat outsourcing is the whole bear case and is genuinely hard to handicap — a 2.4x multiple can be 'correct' if revenue enters terminal decline
Company trimmed its 2026 outlook and guided subdued growth for the rest of FY26; GAAP margins compressed
Meaningful leverage: debt ~$5.5B, D/E 204 — limits flexibility if the top line rolls over
Negative TTM profit margin (-13%); some analysts see only ~1% upside on a neutral rating
catalyst: Evidence that AI is net-additive (seat expansion via iX Suite) rather than deflationary, plus a quarter that arrests the guidance-cut trend
suggested_trade: Small spot only $28-29 as a deep-value AI-fear reversal; keep it starter-sized because the disruption tail risk is real and unquantifiable. Wait for the Sept print before adding.
key_risk: AI genuinely deflates seat-based BPO economics and revenue enters structural decline, in which case the low multiple is a value trap, not a bargain.
would_skip_if: Q3 shows organic revenue turning negative or another guidance cut — that would confirm the AI-erosion thesis.
